I can't imagine how intense the atmosphere would have been.

Checkpoint Charlie was the nickname given to the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point between East Berlin and West Berlin, during the Cold War.

In 1945 the Soviets and Allies agreed that Allied personnel could move freely throughout any sector of Berlin. But in October 1961, just after the Soviets built the wall around West Berlin, the Soviets began stopping Allied diplomatic personnel travelling in the East. During one Allied test of the new Soviet policy, the Americans drove 2 tanks up to the border as a show of force, prompting the Soviets to respond with tanks of their own.

Khrushchev and Kennedy eventually agreed to reduce tensions by withdrawing the tanks. Kennedy offered to go easy over Berlin in the future in return for the Soviets removing their tanks first and the Soviets agreed. Kennedy stated: "It's not a very nice solution, but a wall is a hell of a lot better than a war."
